decisions_needed.not_a_drop_in_because: 29 bp = 6 (-35) + 17 (spacer) + 6 (-10) leaves no room for the UP element upstream of -35 nor the discriminator/ITR downstream of -10; our stage B runs c.run(seq, TSS_range=[0,len(seq)]) on 150 bp tiles yielding ~73 candidate TSSs

measured_here.claim: the NAR core-promoter library is public, downloadable, and is what it claims
measured_here.source_paper: Deep learning guided programmable design of E. coli core promoters from sequence architecture to strength control, Nucleic Acids Research 53(16) gkaf863 (2025), doi 10.1093/nar/gkaf863
measured_here.data_availability_gap: the paper's Data Availability deposits only BioProject PRJNA1189185 (raw NGS, library L4) and a Zenodo code DOI; it does NOT state that the 112,955 measured strengths are released. They are, inside the code repo.
measured_here.architecture: 6 bp (-35 hexamer) + 17 bp spacer + 6 bp (-10 hexamer)
consequences: the paper describes a FIXED 6 bp -10 box (TATAAT); in the released library that holds for only 44.2% of sequences, so the -10 box is a varying position
GC genuinely varies (sd 0.095, span 0.00-0.76), so a GC baseline is non-trivial here and the decomposition-vs-GC question is well posed

reported_model_numbers_on_this_substrate.assay: MBRS (mutation-barcoding-reverse sequencing); 12 bp barcode, mRNA/DNA ratio by amplicon sequencing, validated against sfGFP and qPCR

measured_here.open_gap_the_field_left: the authors used an RNAP-binding-energy matrix (Phillips et al.) to DESIGN the -10/-35 boxes and report R=-0.75 between binding energy and measured strength, but NEVER benchmarked that biophysical model as a predictor against their Transformer. That is the promcalc arm's question, on their substrate, unasked.

findings.headline: two independent 2026 results reproduce this project's encoder-gate negative

our_result.comparison: conv encoder over raw sequence vs ONE GC number

external_1.name: Mechanistic Invariance Test
external_1.benchmark: 650 sequences, 8 classes, E. coli sigma70 promoters, scrambled controls holding composition fixed while moving element position
external_1.authors_reading: misaligned inductive bias, not insufficient capacity; larger models showed STRONGER compositional bias
caveats_from_the_paper_itself: the 46x compositional-over-positional ratio is NOT like-for-like: 21.0 LL units across an AT sweep vs 0.46 LL units across a position sweep, different manipulations, one model
strand-blindness is weaker than it reads: HyenaDNA 44% forward-vs-revcomp has the authors' own binomial p=0.24, supporting 'no better than chance', not 'prefers the wrong strand'
single regulatory system (E. coli sigma70), 100 bp sequences, 5 models, possible training contamination unverifiable
external_1.third_party_flag: a review noted the scrambled controls may not isolate cleanly

external_2.name: Nullsettes
external_2.design: synthetic expression cassettes with control elements translocated so no flanking sequence can rescue expression; 11 eukaryotic / 19 prokaryotic mutant types; 5 MPRA datasets across E. coli, yeast, human
external_2.headline: 9 of 12 below 50% detection on at least one dataset; only Evo2-7B and GENERanno-0.5B strong and consistent
external_2.generanno_efficiency: matched Evo2-7B at 14x fewer parameters and 12x less pretraining data
external_2.quote: Current gLMs recognize what natural expression cassettes look like, but not how they work.
external_2.mechanism: detection depends strongly on the UNMUTATED sequence's likelihood; required threshold scales linearly with length
external_2.scale: no consistent improvement with size within families

findings.why_they_agree: all three say the signal these representations carry on regulatory sequence is COMPOSITIONAL (GC/AT) and that position/mechanism is largely absent; ours via 'a conv encoder does not beat one GC number', the MIT via 'apparent sensitivity is AT-content correlation', Nullsettes via 'detection tracks likelihood, not function'
findings.scale_agreement: ESM2 peaks at 650M and regresses at 3B/15B here; MIT reports stronger compositional bias at larger size; Nullsettes reports no consistent gain with size

findings.headline: the one asymmetry where this project is AHEAD of the published work
findings.result_relevant_to_us: on PROMOTER tasks frozen embeddings recover 95-100% of fine-tuned performance; splice sites far worse at 60-88%
findings.consequence: freezing is NOT the bottleneck for promoter-shaped tasks, which retires 'we should have fine-tuned' as an explanation for our encoder-gate result
findings.the_gap: the paper states it does NOT compare against simple baselines such as GC content or k-mer features, and therefore cannot say whether frozen embeddings outperform hand-built features
findings.our_position: that is precisely the comparison this project ran, paired, multi-seed, CI-reported. Our negative is not a lagging result; it is a measurement the published benchmark is missing.

corroborating.claim: DASHA, 10.5M params, no pretraining, beats all FMs on aggregate across the 18 NT tasks
caveats: FM numbers copied from the NT paper's tables, not re-run
margin driven largely by histone-modification tasks

corroborating.name: Nature Methods 2025
corroborating.claim: deep-learning gene-perturbation prediction does not yet outperform simple linear baselines

counter_example_recorded.name: organism-level-holdout virulence-factor benchmark
counter_example_recorded.numbers: LoRA-fine-tuned DNABERT-2 mean F1 0.18 / AUC 0.54, statistically indistinguishable from k-mer logistic regression AUC 0.51
counter_example_recorded.but: protein-level representations OUTPERFORMED nucleotide models on the same task, so the failure is specific to the NUCLEOTIDE modality, not to learned representations as such

findings.headline: generative DNA: nobody has published a generative foundation model that beats a task-specific designer on wet-lab-measured regulatory activity

sharpest_datum.result: designed enhancers validated by UMI-STARR-seq beat the strongest NATURAL sequence by >2x, and still came in 45% BELOW the top DREAM-challenge-designed sequence

classes.detail: 50 bp E. coli promoters from noise, >90% called real by an independent recognizer, wet-lab validated driving a lysis protein with phase-specific tunable lysis, no auxiliary discriminator

classes.approach: conditional diffusion + validated predictor (the NAR platform)
classes.relevance: pairs a generator with a validated oracle, which is our own design-scored-by-oracle shape

classes.detail: E. coli promoter design, in-vivo activity for a majority of designs

classes.approach: RL fine-tuning of an AR gLM (ICLR 2025, HyenaDNA + RL)
classes.detail: yeast promoters / human enhancers; frames offline-MBO vs active learning

classes.approach: Dirichlet flow matching / GFlowNets / score-conditioned generators

classes.detail: Evo 2 40B, 1 Mb context, 9.3T bp, Nature Mar 2026; a 20B variant Feb 2026 fits a single H100
classes.relevance: still not a T4; CLAUDE.md's hosted-API-only note stands

classes.detail: Nature 2026-01-28, SOTA on 22/24 track and 25/26 variant-effect tasks, API-available
classes.relevance: confirms the standing read that the training method transfers and the architecture does not

findings.actionable_shape: every generative success above is SMALL, TASK-SPECIFIC and PAIRED WITH A VALIDATED ORACLE: diffusion over a short window, scored by a predictor fit on real measurements. That is the architecture this project already argued for from the oracle-selection result. The un-pulled lever is not a bigger pretrained model.

cheaper_model_note.why: matched Evo2-7B on Nullsettes at 14x fewer params and 12x less data; materially cheaper than the 1.2B pin if a learned representation is ever revisited

does_not_support: does NOT reopen the GLM encoder gate; two external agreements are reason to trust the negative more, not to re-run it
does NOT predict the promcalc verdict; the pre-registered bar is unchanged and the reconcile gate remains the validity anchor (gc_seed0 already passed at exactly 0.3000)
is a SCAN, not a systematic review: ~12 searches and ~12 fetches, biased toward prokaryotic promoters and generative design
three fetches were blocked (ScienceDirect 403, PMC cookie wall x2, Nature IDP redirect), so the virulence-factor and Nature Communications benchmark numbers rest on search summaries

the MIT and Nullsettes results are single un-replicated studies; the MIT is a workshop paper with a third-party flag on its controls. Their direction agrees with our own independent measurement, which is why they are load-bearing here, not their authority.
